sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Thursday at 7,730.99, near the top of its one-month range (7,316-7,799) - about 0.9% off the recent high. The Nasdaq-100 sits in similar territory at 29,641.56 against a one-month band of 27,192-30,085, roughly 1.5% below its peak. The VIX has drifted to the low end of its own one-month range, closing at 14.5 versus a high near 20.7 three weeks back - a calmer tape heading into the week ahead. Fifteen SP500/R1000/core names report this week, concentrated in technology (11 of 15), with industrials and consumer-defensive rounding out the calendar.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Monday: Walmart (WMT US) opens the week reporting into consumer-defensive, a group running a median -0.54% reaction on recent prints. Tuesday brings MongoDB (MDB US) and Palo Alto Networks (PANW US), both technology - the week's most-represented sector at 11 of 15 names, median +0.45%. Wednesday is the heaviest day: Broadcom (AVGO US) reports alongside AeroVironment (AVAV US), the latter in industrials, this week's sharpest-moving sector at median -1.38%. Thursday closes with Copart (CPRT US), also industrials, and Dell (DELL US) in technology.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table at +6.62% median across 151 tickers, backed by a thick news window of 2,626 items. Oil-gas sits at the other end, -2.15% median across 33 names with 1,007 news items - also a thick window. Copper is smaller but sharper: +2.63% median on just 6 tickers and 247 news items, a tighter, less-diluted read.
